about: Couple and journal prompts. Prompts with weeks are mapped to pregnancy weeks; prompts with stages serve those stages after or before pregnancy and rotate by calendar week (learn.go CoupleTalkPrompts). Our own writing, no health claims, so no sources.

prompts.text: When did it first feel real for each of you? Tell the story from your side.
Write down how you found out, while the details are still fresh.
Which traditions from your own childhoods do you want to keep, and which would you quietly drop?
What kind of parent do you hope to be? Three words are enough.
Who do we tell, when, and how? Make a short list together.
Each write five names you love, then swap lists. Circle one from the other's list.
Describe the first family trip you imagine taking with the baby.
What did your parents get right? What do you want to do differently?
How do we each feel about finding out the sex before the birth, or keeping it a surprise?
Start a letter to the baby. Tell them about the world they are coming into this month.
Which songs or books do we want the baby to hear from us first?
How much leave can each of us take, and how do we want to stagger it?
Write about the first time you felt or saw the baby move. Where were you?
What will the nursery corner look like? Pick one thing each that has to be there.
Who are the three people we can call at 2 a.m. if we need help?
What are you most looking forward to about the first month? What are you least sure about?
What should the baby call each of our parents? Ask them what they would like.
Which chores does each of us own today, and which will change after the birth?
Write a note to yourself to read on the hardest night of the first month.
How do we want to split nights in the first weeks: shifts, or tasks?
Visitors in the first two weeks: who, how long, and who says no if we are tired?
What do you need to feel rested enough? Write down your non-negotiables.
Finish the letter to the baby together. Each add one paragraph.
What do we each want in the birth room, and what should the partner speak up for?
Shortlist the names. Say each one out loud with our family name. Which feels like them?
Describe your bump, your mood and the room you are sitting in, for the baby to read one day.
Is the hospital bag packed? What is the one thing each of us would forget?
Who walks the dog, feeds the cat or picks up older kids if labor starts at night?
What do we want to do as a couple in the last weeks before the baby comes?
Write down what you hope the first hour with the baby feels like.
What is one thing you love about how your partner is handling this pregnancy?
One line for this week: how are you, really?
What is one thing from your own childhood you want your kid to have too?
Where do you each picture us living when the baby is two? Same place, or somewhere new?
How do we want to handle money once there are three of us: one shared budget, or separate pots plus a shared one?
What would a perfect ordinary Sunday look like for us as a family of three?
Which friends or relatives do we want close by in the first year?
What are you each a little scared of about becoming parents? Just listen, no fixing.
Who in our lives is a parent we admire, and what do they do that we like?
What is one trip or project we want to do as two before a baby arrives?
What was the best small moment with the baby this week, for each of you?
Which night or morning task feels heaviest right now? Could we swap it for a week?
What is one thing the other did this week that made your day easier?
When did you last get an hour just for yourself? Plan one for each of you this week.
Who has offered help that we have not taken up yet? Pick one thing to say yes to.
What does the baby do now that they did not do a month ago?
Which visits or plans this week can we skip without guilt?
What do we want to remember about this stage? Write down one line each.
What made the little one laugh hardest this week?
Which rule do we want to hold the same way, both of us? Agree on the words you will use.
What is one routine that is working well right now, and what makes it work?
When did each of you feel most patient this week, and when least?
What new word or trick from this week do we want to write down?
Which weekend outing would all of us enjoy?
What question from our child this week surprised you most?
Which friend does our child talk about most? What do they like about them?
What is one chore our child could take over, and how will we cheer it on?
When was the last calm bedtime, and what made it work?
What do we each want our child to remember from this year?
Which worry of theirs came up this week, and how did we each answer it?
Plan one small tradition for this month: a walk, a pancake morning, a library day.
What did you each love doing at this age? Could we try it with them?
What did our child say about school or friends this week that stuck with you?
Which activity seems to light them up, and which feels like a chore to them?
How are screens fitting into our week? Is there anything we want to change together?
What is one thing our child did on their own this week that we can praise?
When does each of us get one-on-one time with them? Plan one for this week.
What small goal is our child working toward, and how can we each help?
